title: How many of you guys use a custon AI-made engine? If so, how?
author: More-Drink2211
selftext:
Question popped up in my mind right now, and considering the capabilities of modern frontier models, there has to be someone who has already made a custom game engine instead of using Unity or Godot.

I'm not exactly a game dev expert, at most, I've just dabbled a bit in Blender modelling every now and then, and thats about it. 

How many of you guys use a custom AI-made game engine instead of Unreal/Unity/Godot etc? If so, how did you make it?

comments.author: Legal_Suggestion4873
comments.body:
I do. Just tell it to make you one. Figure out what you want and let 'er rip.

If you don't know what to ask for, you have to learn. Simple as that.

Mine works really well! I think its much faster than Unreal at this point.

Though, I'm not sure if it was \*really\* worth it. Hard to say. Maybe just going to something like Godot or Unity would've been better, or figuring out how to work with Unreal more. Unreal just has so much blueprint stuff and is so slow due to the editor and such. But maybe it would've been better to power through and just try to make existing systems work. 

The models have all been trained on the major engines, which is a benefit I think.

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body: Somewhat custom. I built an in-game map editor with my own assets. That way I can mold and build my stages with settings that conforms to the game and my needs and not all that extra fluff.

comments.author: Dexter1272
comments.body: I am trying to do custom engine with claude recently . I am wondering how it turns out... but for now it is ok. I've got baked lightning, net code with prediction, lag compensation, jolt physics.

comments.author: Initial_Plastic_8069
comments.body: hm mthis is interesting, but lets suppose we want ot sell this game with this speific engine to steam, playstore or whateve,r would it be problematic ? I am not knowlegable

replies.author: iliadz
replies.body: It would not. Basically the engine builds the exe in the end. In godot, I have modified the engine, mainly to allow custom encyrption of my game, and to deter reverse engineering. It will eventually be reverse engineered if it becomes even a tiny bit popular, but this would slow down the process to make it a bit harder :)

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body:
Mine is a node based editor, I add features to it as needed so that I can build the game how I want. it is highly flexible and moddable so that any player can access it and build thier own custom weapons, ships, enemies, maps or really anything else if they want.

Its actually a smarter way to build a game this way because it stops the AI from messing you about as much if you have full access to make changes, edit content ect.  it does require an understanding of gameplay, programing structure, logic and execution flow but yeah its extremely powerful

https://i.redd.it/8e6w5ihpqt2i1.gif

I built it based on my usage of unreal engine and comfyUI which both have powerful node systems.

comments.author: FragmentedHeap
comments.body:
One piece at a time.  Extremely modularly. 

I've been working on it for about 2 months on multiple claude 200 resets. 

A good engine is many millions of lines of code and does not fit in a context so if you just ask it to build you an engine it's going to drift and become unmaintainable pretty quick. 

So I break it down into individual components like text rendering as its own project.  The web GPU layer is also its own project.  Sound is its own project.  Window management is its own project.  And so on. 

I create a very modular core that's many many projects that I'll get used as pieces in the engine.

comments.author: Latent_Space_Cadet
comments.body: You should definitely try to make your own UE or even Godot.  Just try to one-shot it.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
I’ve done it both ways. For most projects, a pre-made engine is way better, hands down. It’s not even close.

There are legitimate reasons to make your own engine for your game. Just keep in mind that all of the stuff like level editors, porting, weird text and UI stuff, the ability to handle a zillion different controllers… if you make your own engine, you’re gonna be burning a ton of credits to play catch up with an existing engine.

comments.author: ResponsibleStudent74
comments.body:
I would say I have developed a custom AI-Assisted engine - I started building my engine about 2-years ago, from scratch - simply because I have a unique genre of games that I like and want to create and it was a way for me to practice my coding skills in general.  I've used the bigger engines for other projects, but this definitely was more of a passion project for me.  

Using AI just help speed up some of the base coding work - and I can go in and refine it or add to the existing logic - just like I do in my day-to-day job (25+year software engineer) - I use AI the same way, I have been using code generators tools at work for the last decade - the mundane or general stuff, i push off to AI - and the validation and refinement I do myself.

Just for argument sake - I asked my Agent to breakdown the contributions to the engine and it gave me this:

https://i.redd.it/sxu655ywvt2i1.png

I think that's a reasonable trade-off.

comments.author: Gigaslavx
comments.body: It's overthinking. Just make a fun game. Custom engine, why not custom OS? Not saying one shot slop with 3rd party assets but there gotta be a balance

comments.author: LiquidZebra
comments.body:
AI is extremely homebrew oriented. It will flat out say your own buggy dogshit of an engine is better than anything you suggest. 

It wants you to keep paying for subs

comments.author: HuWeiliu
comments.body: Use Godot but told it to make C modules for a bunch of the game when suitable as its much much much faster than GScript or whatever Godot uses.

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body: i don’t understand why anyone would bother to make an engine now

comments.author: JjyKs
comments.body:
Yes. I feel that AI handles it way better when it has full access to the source that's not bloated by stuff that the game doesn't need. This is completely custom C++ engine that exports to mobile, webgpu and desktop.
